title: An adaptor for feedback regulation of heme biosynthesis by a mitochondrial protease.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran the context script (no accessions found beyond four UniProt protein identifiers and lab reagent RRIDs; no GEO/SRA/BioProject/PRIDE/Zenodo/Dryad hits). Europe PMC refuses full text and the supplementary-file endpoint because the article is not open access. Read the complete PubMed Central author-manuscript HTML (65,000 characters: abstract, results, figure legends, full methods, data availability). Probed both PMC download paths for the single supplementary spreadsheet (Table S1, 1 MB .xlsx): the pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov /bin/ path returns a 1,817-byte HTML challenge page instead of the file, the www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov path returns 404. Also probed the bioRxiv preprint (10.1101/2024.07.05.602318) supplementary page, which returned an empty error.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the experiments: that the measurements are in-vitro degradation time courses of recombinant ALAS2 by CLPX-CLPP read out on stained gels (n = 2-5 replicates per condition), Western blots of ALAS1/ALAS2 in HEK293 and mouse erythroleukaemia cells, flow-cytometry protoporphyrin IX histograms, heme Soret-band spectra, and AlphaFold2-multimer / AlphaFold3 predicted complexes. The contents of Table S1 are unknown because the file could not be downloaded.

a1_downloadable.note: No data is deposited anywhere: the statement reads 'All data contributing to the conclusions presented are included in the manuscript or the supplementary materials', and the context script found no repository accession. The only tabular supplement (Table S1, 1 MB .xlsx) would not download: PMC's binary path returns a challenge page and Europe PMC refuses the article as not open access. Checked, not assumed.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Any label (whether a protein is degraded by CLPX-CLPP, or how fast) exists only as gel images and fitted rates reported inside figure panels, so it would have to be constructed by hand from the figures. Read in the paper; the file could not be opened to check.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs for a sequence model would be protein sequences, and the paper gives UniProt accessions for all four proteins (P22557 ALAS2, Q9Y2S7 POLDIP2, O76031 CLPX, Q16740 CLPP), so sequences are a trivial lookup. Read in the paper.

a4_units_stated.note: The methods state units clearly (micromolar protein concentrations, millimolar ATP-gamma-S, degradation rates from linear fits, mean fluorescence intensity). Read in the methods text, not verified in a file.

a5_enough_rows.note: The entire quantitative output is a few dozen degradation time courses and blots with n = 2, 3 or 5 replicates each (the only replicate numbers stated anywhere in the paper), plus a handful of flow-cytometry conditions. That is orders of magnitude below the ~1,500-row bar. Read in figure legends; no file opened.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~1 MB (one spreadsheet) plus four protein sequences
a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small, but small for the wrong reason: there is no dataset, not a compact one.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked at all: no file was retrievable, so there is nothing to compare against the paper's numbers.

a8_label_provenance.note: Where labels exist they come from real physical measurements (gel densitometry of degradation, immunoblots, fluorescence), not from another model's output. The AlphaFold2/AlphaFold3 complexes in the paper are predictions, so they could only ever be features, never labels.

existing_models.name: deepDegron (deep-learning predictor of degrons, the short sequence elements that trigger protein destruction, trained on high-throughput global protein stability assays)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved; only the documentation site and GitHub page were seen in search results, so no number is quoted here.

existing_models.name: MetaDegron (protein language model predicting degrons targeted by E3 ubiquitin ligases, Briefings in Bioinformatics, 2024)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved beyond the search abstract; no number quoted.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Search abstract states only a limited number of degron instances are known, implying label scarcity is the open problem.

existing_models.name: Degpred (BERT-based proteome-wide degron predictor, BMC Biology, 2022) and DegronMD (degron knowledgebase reporting >18,000 new degrons)
Machine-learning classifiers of fast-degrading proteins in Escherichia coli (mSystems, 2021), using structural, physicochemical and interaction-network features
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved; the abstract reports that physicochemical and network features beat known degron motifs, without a number I verified.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Implied: sequence degron motifs alone do not predict degradation.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (protein language model, small CPU-runnable checkpoints)
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU would be plenty, but there are no labelled examples to fit a head on.
backbone.licence: MIT (permissive) for ESM-2; irrelevant here because no training data exists.

integration.partner_dataset: Human cytosolic degron maps and global protein stability screens (for example the near-complete human cytosolic degron map in Science Advances 2026, and the data behind deepDegron), joined to this paper's four proteins by UniProt accession.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do the sequence features that make a protein unstable in the cytosol also predict destruction by the mitochondrial CLPX-CLPP protease, or does the mitochondrion use a different code? — a real question, but this paper contributes only four proteins to it, so the join has nothing to carry.

controls.positive_control: None available: with a handful of conditions there is no held-out signal a model could be required to recover.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is meaningless at n = 2-5 per condition.
controls.external_validation: Global protein stability / degron datasets exist externally, but this paper supplies no comparable measurements to validate against them.

honest_claim_h3: No model can be trained from this paper: the honest claim would be limited to 'POLDIP2 and heme-bound ALAS2 are predicted by AlphaFold to interact through the cysteine-proline motif', which is a restatement of the paper's own figure, not a prediction.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein sequence to predict which mitochondrial proteins the CLPX-CLPP protease chops up when heme is abundant.
plain_idea.train_on: Would need many protein sequences each labelled as degraded or spared by the CLPX-CLPP protease; this paper provides roughly a few dozen measured conditions covering four proteins and some truncation variants, so effectively zero training examples.
plain_idea.predict: Whether, and how fast, a protein is destroyed by CLPX-CLPP. The true answer here comes from densitometry of stained gels in reconstituted reactions and from immunoblots in cultured cells, with 2-5 replicates per condition.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups studying erythropoietic protoporphyria (a disease of excess porphyrin caused by broken heme-pathway feedback) would like to know which patient mutations block this degradation step, but the data to learn that does not exist in this paper.

more_or_better_data.why: Existing degron predictors were trained on high-throughput stability screens covering thousands of sequences (deepDegron) or thousands of proteins (the near-complete human cytosolic degron map, 5,672 proteins per its abstract); this paper offers four proteins and some truncations.

confidence_score.why: Replicates exist (n = 2-5 per condition) so noise could in principle be estimated, but with only a few dozen conditions there is no way to calibrate per-prediction confidence.

models_beatable.why: The relevant models are recent (Degpred 2022, MetaDegron 2024) and at least one is open and runnable (deepDegron), and we have no data with which to beat them.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition outright: we have no training set, so the existing model cannot be used as a baseline for anything of ours.

ml_idea: The only idea the biology suggests — predict CLPX-CLPP (mitochondrial caseinolytic protease) substrates and heme-conditional degrons from protein sequence using a frozen protein language model — would have to be built almost entirely from other people's high-throughput stability data, with this paper contributing four proteins as anecdotes. That is a different project about a different dataset.

effort.compute_note: No compute estimate is meaningful because there is no feature/label table to build; the only file is a 1 MB spreadsheet that would not download.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the data availability statement and count the replicates in the figure legends: 'all data are in the manuscript or supplementary materials', n = 2-5 per condition. That took ten minutes and killed it.

verdict_reason: A classic single-mechanism biochemistry paper with no deposited dataset. The data availability statement points only to the manuscript and one 1 MB supplementary spreadsheet, which PMC would not serve (binary path blocked, Europe PMC refuses the non-open-access article), and the quantitative content is a few dozen in-vitro degradation time courses and blots at n = 2-5 replicates covering four proteins. Fails A1 (nothing deposited and the one file is not retrievable), A2 (any degradation label lives in figure panels and would have to be reconstructed), A5 (far under 1,500 rows) and A7 (no file to count). The conclusions are valuable biology; they are not a machine-learning substrate.
